description_full: Gravity Co., Ltd. develops and publishes online and mobile games worldwide. It offers massively multiplayer online role-playing games, including Ragnarok Online, Dragonica, Requiem Online, R.O.S.E. Online, Ragnarok Online II, and Ragnarok Landverse, as well as character-based merchandise and animation. Its mobile games portfolio includes Ragnarok M; Eternal Love; Ragnarok Origin; Ragnarok X: Next Generation; Ragnarok Arena; WITH ISLAND; the Labyrinth of Ragnarok; Ragnarok Poring; Tera Classic; NBA: Rise To Stardom; Generation Zombie; Ragnarok Idle Adventure; Ragnarok 20 Heroes; White Chord; WITH: Whale In The High; Ragnarok Lost Memories; and Paladog Tactics. It also provides console games, such as Ragnarok DS for Nintendo DS; Ragnarok: The Princess of Light and Darkness for PlayStation Portable; Ragnarok Odyssey for PlayStation Vita; Double Dragon II for Xbox 360; Ragnarok Odyssey Ace for PlayStation Vita and PlayStation 3; Pigromance for Steam, Stove, Nintendo Switch, Xbox One, Xbox Series X|S; ALTF4 11 for Steam and Stove; Wetory for Steam, Stove, Nintedo Switch; and GRANDIA HD Collection for Nintendo Switch. In addition, it offers games for IPTV, including Haunted House and Pororo: The Little Penguin, and Kongsuni; and markets dolls, stationery, food, and other character-based merchandise, as well as game manuals, monthly magazines, and other publications; PC games, including Puzzle, Platformer, ALTF4 II, Ragnarok ZERO, KAMiBAKO-Mythology of Cube, Psychodemic, and FINAL KNIGHT; social network games and mobile games, such as Ragnarok V: Returns, Ragnarok: The Lost Memories and Ragnrok Begins in-house; and web-browser-based games, such as Ragnarok Prequel and Ragnarok Prequel II. Further, the company provides system development and maintenance services, as well as system integration services to third parties. The company was incorporated in 2000 and is headquartered in Seoul, South Korea. Gravity Co., Ltd. is a subsidiary of GungHo Online Entertainment, Inc.

financial_summary: GRAVITY Co., Ltd. is a small-cap communication services business with a $467M market cap on $44M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +1% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory. Operating margins are expanding by +13.9pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.

Returns on capital run at -42% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, and 20% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $2M in free cash flow — roughly 4 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 9.71× so those profits are backed by real cash.

On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and thin -4307.2× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 4.8% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 59% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and profit capture is only 0.3× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.

sect: Its 7% operating margin is roughly in line with the Communication Services median (9%).
It captures well under its share of sector profits (0.32x its revenue share).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.06 across 169 companies in the universe; the top four hold 36% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares have drifted higher, up 16% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 12% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 33% and a beta of 0.87, it moves roughly with the market.
About $1.6M trades a day, enough to build a position.
In past sell-offs it fell 41% in the 2020 crash, 48% in the 2022 bear market and 85% in 2008.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $12.24 (margin of safety -449%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 65%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $10.22 to $15.28 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
Multiples send mixed signals against Communication Services peers: cheaper on P/E 7.9 vs 14.9, richer on P/FCF 240.2 vs 11.3 (sector median).
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 0.4% (below the risk-free rate).
prof: ROIC of 42% falls short of the cost of capital of 9.1%, so growth at these returns destroys value.
It runs a 20% gross margin and converts 4% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 7/9.
ROE of 1% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.8x equity multiplier).
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $32.1M (7% of market cap).
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 14.1, in the safe zone).
growth: Revenue has compounded at 0.5% over 3 years, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 26%).
Capex runs only 0.4x depreciation (0.3% of sales), so the asset base is being harvested rather than grown.
own: Insiders own 59.3%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 17%.
It returns 4.8% a year to shareholders (4.8% in dividends).
people: With about 437 employees, each generates about $102K of revenue, 0.2x the Communication Services median.
That works out to $4K of free cash flow per employee.
